claim_text: An unauthorized third party got into Roll20's system
summary: Roll20's CTO says that on the evening of Nov 16 an unauthorized third party gained access to its system and reached some account information.
detail: This is the company's own account on its official forum. It calls it a 'security incident' that has been contained.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's own notice says an unauthorized third party gained access to its system.

claim_text: The way in was a flaw in a system that processed animated image uploads
summary: Privacy Affairs quotes Roll20's email to users: an unauthorized third party 'exploited a vulnerability in one of our systems that processed animated image uploads'.
detail: We have not seen the email itself; Privacy Affairs read it in a recipient's public post. Roll20's forum notice says only that the 'pathway' is fixed. Which software had the flaw is not known.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Privacy Affairs quotes the email's 'What happened' section word for word.

summary: Roll20 says it believes the attack was part of a global trend of automated, AI-assisted attacks on organizations large and small.
detail: Roll20 has not said what makes it think AI was involved, and no one else has shown it.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Roll20 states the belief; Privacy Affairs notes it gave no basis for it.

summary: No person or group has been named, and we found no public claim of responsibility.
detail: Roll20 describes only an 'unauthorized third party'.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Neither the notice nor the coverage names an attacker.

claim_text: Roll20 found the access on the evening of Nov 16 and blocked it
summary: Roll20 says it learned of the access on the evening of Nov 16, 2026, blocked it immediately and started a full investigation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's notice gives the date and says access was blocked at once.

summary: Roll20 says it emailed each affected user directly, and that anyone who did not get an email was not involved.
detail: Privacy Affairs says the first users posted about the email around 12:50 PM ET on Nov 20, before the forum notice.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's notice says it emailed each affected user; Privacy Affairs gives the timing.

claim_text: Roll20's CTO posted the notice on Nov 20
summary: Roll20's chief technology officer posted 'Security Update: November 2026' on the company's forum at 1:37 PM ET on Nov 20.
detail: The forum shows the post was edited later that afternoon. Replies are closed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The post's own time stamp on Roll20's forum.

claim_text: Roll20 says it has fixed the way in
summary: Roll20 says it has fixed the pathway used in the incident and has increased its spending on security.
detail: No outside check of the fix has been published.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's notice states the fix in its own words.

claim_text: Fewer than 1% of Roll20 users were affected
summary: Roll20 says fewer than 1% of its users were potentially affected.
detail: Roll20 has not given a number of accounts.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's own figure in its notice.

summary: Privacy Affairs estimates up to about 150,000 accounts, from Roll20's claim of more than 15 million players.
detail: This is an outlet's estimate, not a company figure.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The figure is Privacy Affairs' own arithmetic, not a disclosed count.

claim_text: Names, email addresses and password hashes were involved
summary: Roll20 says affected accounts' information included first and last names, email addresses and a salted bcrypt hash of each password.
detail: Roll20 says 'details such as', so the list may not be complete. A hash is a scrambled form of the password; strong unique passwords stay hard to guess, weak or reused ones less so.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's notice lists these data types.

claim_text: Last four card digits for some users; no full card numbers
summary: Roll20 says a much smaller group with a saved card also had the card's last 4 digits involved. Full card numbers, security codes, expiry dates and billing addresses were not.
detail: Roll20 says it does not hold full card details; its payment processors do.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20's notice says which card data was and was not involved.

claim_text: Roll20 says it found no evidence the data was copied or misused
summary: Roll20 says its investigation found no evidence that the data was copied or misused.
detail: No evidence of copying is not proof that nothing was copied, and no outside review has been published.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Roll20 states the finding; Privacy Affairs repeats it with the same caveat.

claim_text: Whether IP addresses or other data were involved
summary: Roll20's notice does not mention IP addresses or other data types; Privacy Affairs says it has asked.
detail: Roll20 named last known IP addresses in its 2024 breach.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The notice is silent; the outlet says the question is open.

claim_text: Roll20 has had earlier breaches, in 2018 and 2024
summary: Privacy Affairs reports a 2018 breach of almost 4 million accounts and a June 2024 admin-account takeover that exposed names, emails and card digits.
detail: This is background from one outlet; we have not re-read Roll20's 2024 notice.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Privacy Affairs lists both earlier incidents with their data types.

claim_text: A link to this week's outages
summary: Nothing connects the Roll20 breach to this week's national outages; no source suggests it.
label: Not established

claim_text: Roll20's advice: two-factor sign-in and a unique password
summary: Roll20 tells users to turn on two-factor authentication and use a password they use nowhere else, and says it will never ask for a password.
label: Confirmed
